dateNote: Public weight release August 26, 2026; initial repository placeholder August 25.
subtitle: How compact memory and constrained depth mixing fit together
summary: GLM-5.3-Flash combines sparse and linear attention with manifold-constrained hyper-connections in a multimodal base model.
lead: An efficient model must decide both how to retain a long conversation and how to pass representations through many layers. GLM-5.3-Flash changes both structures, combining a hybrid attention stack with constrained mixing among multiple residual streams.

sections.title: A new base rather than only a new tuning run
sections.html:
The official model card describes GLM-5.3-Flash as the first natively multimodal model in the GLM-5 series. It lists 320 billion total parameters, 18 billion active, and a new base trained with a 30-trillion-token multimodal corpus. It explicitly names hybrid sparse/linear attention and manifold-constrained hyper-connections, abbreviated mHC.

[1]

The distinction from GLM-5.3 matters: the family repository says that the larger 5.3 model reused the 5.2 base and gained through post-training. Flash is a different architecture, not merely that same model served with a faster setting.

[2]

A name can conceal several experiments. Post-training changes which behaviors existing representations support. A new base can change how information is represented, stored and mixed before those behaviors are taught. Comparing the two requires examining their configurations, not interpreting the word “Flash” as a technical specification.

sections.title: Three compact updates, then sparse retrieval
sections.html:
The released configuration contains 45 layers: eleven groups of three linear-attention layers followed by one DeepSeek sparse-attention layer, then one final linear layer. That makes 34 linear layers and 11 sparse-attention layers. The linear layers update state; sparse attention retains a selected-retrieval route. The configuration names the linear-layer indices kda_layers and exposes sparse-indexer settings. A configuration identifies the chosen layout; it does not by itself explain every detail of the implemented kernels. These are inspectable properties of the released checkpoint, rather than deductions from a benchmark chart.

[3]

Think of processing a long technical manual. A running summary may preserve the current subject, but a later question might require a particular serial number. Direct retrieval and compression have complementary roles. The illustration does not assume that the real model separates them into human-readable tasks.

The widget counts a toy fixed state beside a history that stores 64 scalars per token. Increasing context length only grows the second count. In the actual hybrid, the retrieval layers still retain context-dependent storage, so a fixed recurrent-state count does not imply fixed memory for the entire model. Selecting fewer cached entries for attention is also different from discarding all entries outside a sliding window.

figure.title: One stack can contain two memory regimes
figure.caption: Illustrative scalar counts, not an estimate of GLM-5.3-Flash memory.
figure.takeaway: Hybrid attention reduces some history costs while retaining a retrieval path.

sections.title: Constrain the mixing so signals do not grow freely
sections.html:
A residual stream carries representations between layers. Hyper-connections widen that route into multiple streams and learn how to mix them. The mHC component paper, from DeepSeek, targets a doubly stochastic residual mixing matrix: entries are nonnegative, and each row and column sums to one. Repeated row and column normalization, called Sinkhorn–Knopp iteration, approximates that constraint in a finite number of steps. GLM adopts this prior mechanism.

[4]

An exactly normalized two-stream teaching example makes the target constraint tangible. Begin with values 2 and 8. Mix using rows [0.75, 0.25] and [0.25, 0.75]. The outputs are 3.5 and 6.5. Each is a convex mixture of the inputs, and their sum stays 10. Apply the same matrix again and the outputs become 4.25 and 5.75.

Compare unrestricted rows [1, 1] and [1, 1]. The same inputs become 10 and 10, then 20 and 20. Repeating that mixing amplifies the signal. Constraining the connection matrix controls this pathway; it does not by itself prove that every nonlinear operation in the complete network is stable.

figure.title: Control the route between layers
figure.caption: Simplified mHC concept using a two-stream arithmetic example; the released config uses four streams.
figure.takeaway: Restrictions on the connection matrix can control repeated signal mixing.

sections.title: Read capabilities and mechanisms separately
sections.html:
The released configuration’s hc_mult value is four, and hc_sinkhorn_iters is 20. The latter is a finite approximation to the ideal normalization, not proof of exact row and column sums in floating-point computation. Configuration files establish chosen dimensions and switches; they cannot establish that a model understands a photograph or solves a software task reliably.

[3]

That second claim needs evaluation. For a visual task, change the evidence in the image and check whether the answer changes appropriately. For a coding task, run the repaired program against meaningful tests. For a long-context task, place relevant facts at several distances and include distractors.

The architecture suggests which costs to measure: recurrent-state storage, sparse cache and indexing, expert movement, and residual-stream traffic. The improvements may interact, so whole-system performance should be measured rather than inferred by multiplying favorable ratios from separate components.
